discovery.capacity: 38,544 (official MLB/Twins figure, 2019-present). Other published figures: 39,504 (ballparksofbaseball.com), 39,021 (andrewclem.com), ~40,000 (Minnesota Ballpark Authority). Standing room adds ~2,500. Use 38,544 as the authoritative number.

orientation.batter_faces: Batter/home plate faces out toward center field to the EAST-NORTHEAST (roughly 45-90 deg true; Wikipedia states the diamond is 'aligned east', andrewclem.com lists CF orientation 'E (45)' i.e. northeast). Geography corroborates NE: Gate 14 (home plate) sits on 7th St N on the southwest side, Gate 3 (center field) at 5th St & 3rd Ave on the northeast side. Consequence: the FIRST BASE / RIGHT FIELD side faces southeast toward downtown Minneapolis, and the THIRD BASE side seats are the ones that look across at the Minneapolis skyline.
orientation.confidence: CONFIRMED direction is easterly/northeasterly; UNCERTAIN on the exact bearing. theshadium.com claims 'due east 90 deg, third base = north side', which conflicts with the gate geography and with the well-documented fact that the skyline view is FROM the third base side; treat theshadium as lower quality.

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE toward THIRD BASE / LEFT FIELD and DECREASE toward FIRST BASE / RIGHT FIELD. Standing at home plate looking at the field, numbers rise from right to left. This holds on every level and for the lettered club sections too: the 1-17 dugout/Champions series, the 101-140 Main Level, the A-V club letters, the 201-240 Terrace Level and the 301-334 View Level all run the same way (counter-clockwise as seen from above, i.e. right-field foul pole -> first base line -> home plate -> third base line -> left field). IMPORTANT WRAP-AROUND: on the Main Level the series does not stop at the left field corner. It continues all the way around the outfield: 128-131 Left Field Bleachers -> (batter's eye / Delta Sky360 in dead center, no numbered seats) -> 132-135 Treasure Island Cove in right-center/right field -> 136-138 The Overlook in right field -> 139-140 Corona Porch on the right field line, closing the loop back near section 101. So 132-140 are RIGHT field despite being higher numbers than the left field 128-131. This is the single biggest gotcha at Target Field. The 200 and 300 levels do NOT wrap: their outfield sections (229-240, 329-334, the Home Run Porch) stay in LEFT field.

accessibility.summary: Accessible seating is available on ALL levels and at all price points, sold first-come first-served; every gate at Target Field is wheelchair accessible. Roughly 820 disability-accessible seats. Guests who need accessible seating but do not use a wheelchair are given padded folding chairs. Companion seating is sold alongside wheelchair spaces. Order by phone at 1-800-33-TWINS / 612-33-TWINS or online at twins.com/tickets, which has a 'click here for real-time ADA/handicap seating' link. Wheelchair storage is available at Guest Service Centers. Accessible drop-off is on 7th Street near the New Era Team Store and Gate 14. A UnitedHealthcare Sensory Suite for neuroatypical guests is on the Premier Suite Level. Note the Minnesota Ballpark Authority states wheelchair sight lines were designed so users see the full field.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: MIXED, but overwhelmingly NUMBERS. Rows are NUMBERED in essentially the whole ballpark - Main Level (e.g. 115 rows 1-24 then WC-27 and 25-WC; 117 rows 1-24, 25-28; 101 rows 10-40, 41-44; 127 rows 5-35; 128 rows 1-12, 13-15; 131 rows 1-16; 132/135 rows 1-4; 138 rows 1-7), Thrivent Club letters A-V (rows 1-12; Skyline Deck S rows 1-14), Terrace Level (201 rows 1-8; 204/215/228 rows 1-6; 229 rows 1-7; 240 rows 1-12) and View Level (301/304/315 rows 1-14; 334 rows 1-16). THE EXCEPTION: the UnitedHealthcare Champions Club (sections 7-10) uses LETTERED rows - 'Rows in Champions Club 8 are labeled A-M'. Also note Main Level home-plate sections interleave wheelchair rows labeled 'WC' into the numeric sequence (section 115: '1-24, WC-27, 25-WC'). Row 1 is the row closest to the field in the outfield/upper sections, but several sections do not start at row 1 (101 starts at row 10, 127 at row 5, Dugout Boxes around row 5). Entrances are typically at the BACK row on the Terrace Level and at row 1 on much of the View Level.
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the right" (RateYourSeats, quoted identically on section pages 115, 117, 127, 128, 131, 132, 135, 138, 8, A, G, N, R, S, 201, 204, 215, 240, 301, 304, 315, 334). Ballparkeguides states the same rule as "Seat 1 is always on the right" when facing the field. PRACTICAL READING: seat 1 is on the side of the section that faces the LOWER-numbered adjacent sections - i.e. toward FIRST BASE / RIGHT FIELD on the infield, since section numbers increase toward third base. So in a home-plate section like 115, seat 1 is the first-base-side aisle and the highest seat number is the third-base-side aisle. One documented exception note: in section 101, "Low-number seats (1, 2, etc.) from rows 25-40 have a wall blocking part of their outfield view."
discovery.known_obstructions: NETTING: the official Twins seat map flags protective netting over sections 7-10, 1-6 and 11-17 (field level), 109-119, 105-108 and 120-123, 103-104 and 124-125, with 126 partially covered. Fans in Thrivent Club G and nearby infield club sections report 'looking through the screen'. OVERHANG CUT-OFF: because the upper decks in the outfield are stacked directly on top of the lower deck, upper rows of the outfield sections lose a portion of the playing field, and the overhang blocks the scoreboard and skyline from the back rows of covered sections. Right field corner seats lose a lot of the outfield. Main Level sections 106 and 123 have noticeably less overhead coverage than their neighbors. Section 101 low-numbered seats in rows 25-40 have a wall blocking part of the outfield view. Wikipedia states fewer than 200 seats are formally classified as obstructed view. One left-center field lower bleacher section can be raised like a drawbridge for service vehicles. RAIN / COLD COVERAGE (no roof, cold-weather park - this matters): Target Field has one of the largest canopies in baseball, an enlarged soffit over the upper deck. COVERED: most of the View Level 300 sections (301 rows 8+, 304 rows 4+, 315 rows 3+; 304-315 on the first base side get the best protection); Thrivent Club rows 9+ (A-V); the upper rows of the Main Level infield (Home Plate Box row 13+ and Field Box seats sit generally under the 200-level overhang); Left Field Bleachers 128 rows 3+ under the 200 Level overhang; Treasure Island Cove 132-135 almost entirely under the overhang. EXPOSED: The Overlook 136-138 (completely open-air), Corona Porch 139-140, the entire Home Run Porch Terrace 229-234/237-240, the Budweiser Roof Deck, the front rows of every lower-bowl section, and Main Level 106 and 123. SUN: with the northeasterly orientation the third base side is the more exposed side late in day games and gets sun longest; the first base side shades earlier. The third base side is the side with the downtown Minneapolis skyline view.
uncertain: Capacity varies by source: MLB.com and Wikipedia say 38,544; ballparksofbaseball.com 39,504; andrewclem.com 39,021; Minnesota Ballpark Authority ~40,000. 38,544 is the official current figure.

Exact compass bearing. Wikipedia says 'aligned east'; andrewclem.com lists CF orientation 'E (45)' which reads as northeast; theshadium.com claims due east 90 deg and calls third base the 'north side'. Gate geography (Gate 14/home plate on 7th St SW, Gate 3/center field at 5th & 3rd Ave NE) and the fact that the skyline view is from the third base side both support EAST-NORTHEAST. Not resolved to a single degree value.

RateYourSeats' section index omits 235, 236 and 328, while aviewfrommyseat.com renders the ranges as 201-240 and 301-334. Unclear whether those three sections exist, are non-ticketed, or are simply missing from the RYS index.

Terrace Level (200) and View Level (300) home-plate spans are given as 214-216 and 314-316 by inference. Only 215 and 315 were individually verified as 'behind home plate'; 304 was verified as first base side, so the 300-level home-plate block starts at or after 315.

Which lettered Thrivent Club sections fall on which side is inferred from section G ('behind home plate, slightly toward the Twins dugout') plus the F-K centered grouping and the A/R outer-edge note. Individual pages for A, E, N and R did not state a side.

Concert-only sections: aviewfrommyseat.com lists a 'Concert Floor' of F1-F14 plus a 'Pit'. RateYourSeats' concert chart explicitly warns 'Target Field concert seating charts vary by performance... some sections may be removed or altered for individual shows,' so the floor layout is not stable across shows. No official Twins/Target Field concert map was located.

The 'Legends Landing' vs 'Skyline Deck' naming for sections S-V is inconsistent between sources; ticketiq additionally (and probably wrongly) describes 'Legends Club... in sections A-R' on the third level.
Whether the CATCH premium area has its own ticketed section identifiers - RateYourSeats lists 'All CATCH Sections' as a grouping without itemizing them.
Exact seat counts for the Budweiser Roof Deck vary: 120 fixed seats + 130 SRO (mlb.com guide) vs 150 bleacher seats + 150 SRO (ballparksofbaseball.com).
